questions.prompt: Compare a coarse 8.0 cm screw pitch with a fine 2.0 cm pitch. Calculate and cite the IMA, input force, input distance, ideal input work, and relative load speed for both settings. Explain the pattern.
questions.rubricText:
@[Always] Grading feedback: Evidence must come from the student's calculations for the two specified screw settings. BusyBee scoring: Award points only in 0.5-point increments, including whole points, from 0 to the question maximum. Select a rubric-supported allowed score; never report hundredths such as 2.85/3. Do not average or percentage-scale rubric criteria into an off-grid score. A binary completion rubric still permits only 0 or full credit. Allowed scores for this question: 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2.
a. Full credit: Accurately calculates both screw settings and explains that the finer pitch increases IMA, reduces force, increases handle distance, keeps ideal work at 120 J, and reduces relative load speed. Partial credit: Gives the correct pattern with incomplete or slightly inaccurate calculations. No credit: Gives no usable screw calculations or reverses the tradeoff.

questions.prompt: Write a claim-evidence-reasoning conclusion using your calculations for the screw and at least two other machines. Explain how the machines can keep ideal work at 120 J while changing input force and distance, and explain how mechanical advantage is linked to output speed when input speed is held constant.
questions.rubricText:
@[Always] Grading feedback: Grade the claim, evidence from three machine types, work reasoning, and speed-mechanical-advantage connection. BusyBee scoring: Award points only in 0.5-point increments, including whole points, from 0 to the question maximum. Select a rubric-supported allowed score; never report hundredths such as 2.85/3. Do not average or percentage-scale rubric criteria into an off-grid score. A binary completion rubric still permits only 0 or full credit. Allowed scores for this question: 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3.
a. Full credit: States a clear claim, cites accurate evidence from the screw and two other machines, uses force x distance to explain constant ideal work, and explains that greater IMA lowers output speed for the same input speed. Partial credit: Gives the main tradeoff but lacks enough evidence or one part of the reasoning. No credit: Claims a machine reduces ideal work or says greater IMA increases output speed at the same input speed.
